children: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman raised concerns over the pace of artificial intelligence development at the Global Fintech Fest 2026, referring to recent warnings from an AI researcher about frontier laboratories racing to build self-improving, highly advanced systems. She said such warnings merited closer scrutiny and called for greater institutional accountability around AI safety and alignment.

FM Sitharaman pointed to risks emerging from agentic AI systems and large language models, including their potential misuse in cyberattacks and efforts to influence elections. She said she had raised with the Reserve Bank of India whether a lighter regulatory approach could address these risks without stifling innovation in the fintech sector, and welcomed the RBI’s decision to recognise the United FinTech Forum as a self-regulatory organisation for the industry.

Her remarks followed reports that a researcher who had worked at both Anthropic and OpenAI announced his resignation from Anthropic, citing concerns that leading AI firms were prioritising competition with rivals over responsible development practices. The resignation came months after Anthropic and OpenAI separately disclosed that their models had broken out of controlled testing environments and gained unauthorised access to live computer systems, prompting both companies to pause certain evaluations while strengthening monitoring safeguards.

Beyond AI, Sitharaman used her address to strike an optimistic note on India’s workforce, saying the country’s demographic dividend was already playing out rather than remaining a future prospect. She argued that younger professionals were not waiting for conventional benchmarks to prove their contribution, pointing to their role in software development and enterprise creation as evidence of the trend. "This generation is not waiting for legacy yardsticks to validate their productivity, they're already writing tomorrow's code, building enterprises and proving that India's demographic dividend is an active, unstoppable reality," she said.

"India is experiencing demographic dividend in real time...from building the world's most powerful digital public infrastructure with UPI processing billions of transactions, to standing tall as the fastest-growing major economy and breaking frontiers in space exploration, India is experiencing its demographic dividend in real time. What is here before me is a living reality of our demographic dividend," FM added.

She also questioned critics who, in her view, tended to view India’s demographic advantage with persistent scepticism rather than recognising its ongoing impact. She said, "To borrow the now so famous, in social media at least, expression which the Honorable Prime Minister used, our 'naraz Fufajis' are never short of reasons to doubt India's momentum and capabilities of our youth, spending their time debating in television studios whether the demographic dividend has slipped away or turned into a 'burden'. This is setting the pace for our country to reach Viksit Bharat by 2047. We should celebrate this and not be naysayers."

title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman flags agentic AI, LLM risks from cyberattacks to election interference
